name: N.W.A
hook: The Compton group that put West Coast street reporting at the centre of rap, drew a letter from the FBI, and built 'Straight Outta Compton' on the Amen break.

blurb.age7: A rap group from Compton, near Los Angeles. Their songs about police and their neighbourhood made the FBI angry.
blurb.age13: N.W.A came together in Compton, California, in 1986: Eazy-E, Dr. Dre, Ice Cube, MC Ren, DJ Yella and others. Eazy-E paid for it through his label, Ruthless Records. Their 1988 album Straight Outta Compton described life in their neighbourhood, including police harassment, in blunt language. The FBI wrote a letter to their record company complaining about 'Fuck tha Police'. The title track is built on the Amen break. Ice Cube left in 1989 in a dispute over money, and the group ended in 1991. Eazy-E died of AIDS in 1995.
blurb.adult: N.W.A made West Coast gangsta rap a national force and provoked a federal agency to object to a song's lyrics, a rare direct collision between the state and a record. Dr. Dre, the group's main producer, pleaded no contest in 1991 to assaulting the television host Dee Barnes and was sentenced to probation, and a related civil suit was settled. He has since acknowledged the assault. That is part of the record here. His post-N.W.A production, G-funk and 'The Chronic', is covered at his own entry (`dr-dre`).
